title: Control transition with input movement
statement: Let $H$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, with state set $B$, and let $q,r\in B$ and $m\in\{-1,0,1\}$. Suppose that in state $q$, for every input symbol and every tuple of work-tape symbols, the transition of $H$ moves the input head by $m$, leaves all work tapes and their heads unchanged, emits no output, and enters state $r$. Then for every configuration $c$ on any Boolean input whose state is $q$, one step of $H$ is the configuration obtained by setting its state to $r$, moving its input head by $m$ with boundary clamping, and leaving all its other components unchanged.
